title: When the Milk Did Not Come In — Otsuka Quinolinone Patent & D2 Partial Agonism (Comparator PDB 7VOE), Lactotroph Tonic Dopamine Brake & Hypoprolactinemia, Paired Breast-Milk Relative Infant Dose LC–MS/MS & Perinatal Bipolar Stability

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Most antipsychotics block dopamine D2 receptors and raise prolactin, but aripiprazole is a D2 partial agonist—acting like dopamine on pituitary lactotrophs to *suppress* prolactin and stall postpartum milk supply even while tiny breast-milk levels remain low.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding partial agonism explains a counterintuitive bedside puzzle—why an antipsychotic lowers prolactin instead of raising it—without needlessly destabilizing maternal mental health.
keyTakeaways: Pituitary lactotrophs sit under constant tonic dopamine D2 inhibition; full D2 antagonists cut that brake and cause hyperprolactinemia, whereas partial agonist aripiprazole supplies ~25–30% intrinsic D2 tone and can drive prolactin below lactation thresholds.
Paired maternal serum and breast-milk LC–MS/MS quantifies the Relative Infant Dose (RID) of aripiprazole plus active metabolite dehydroaripiprazole.
Perinatal psychiatry balances infant feeding goals against the high danger of postpartum bipolar relapse.

vocab.meaning: A ligand that binds a receptor with high affinity and produces a moderate sub-maximal response—acting as a brake when endogenous tone is high, or a floor when tone drops.
Anterior pituitary cell that secretes prolactin to drive mammary milk synthesis, normally restrained by hypothalamic dopamine.
The weight-adjusted daily infant drug intake via breast milk expressed as a percentage of the weight-adjusted maternal dose.

quiz.question: Why can aripiprazole cause failure of lactogenesis (low prolactin) when risperidone causes galactorrhea (high prolactin)?
options: Aripiprazole's intrinsic D2 partial agonist activity maintains dopaminergic inhibition on pituitary lactotrophs, suppressing prolactin secretion
Aripiprazole blocks oxytocin synthesis in the kidney
quiz.explanation: Because dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin release, aripiprazole's partial agonist tone mimics dopamine enough at lactotroph D2 receptors to suppress the postpartum prolactin surge.
